subject.title: Fallback turns can re-execute work already reported as completed (semantic recursive task execution)

question: Should the linked PR land as an explicitly scoped embedded-runtime mitigation while this issue tracks the remaining gateway, sessions_send/cron, and Codex-native spawn coverage, or should it wait for one shared work-spawning policy seam?
rationale: The fix path changes fallback-turn delegation policy and intentionally leaves related work-spawning surfaces uncovered, so automation cannot choose the fail-closed boundary or cross-repo Codex scope.

options.title: Accept Scoped Mitigation
options.body: Land or rework the linked PR for embedded sessions_spawn and keep this issue open for the remaining surfaces.

options.title: Require Shared Seam First
options.body: Hold the linked PR until one policy covers OpenClaw tools and Codex-native delegation consistently.

options.title: Split Follow-Ups First
options.body: Keep the linked PR paused until maintainers identify separate owner-backed follow-up items for each uncovered surface.

recommendation.title: Accept Scoped Mitigation
recommendation.body: Land or rework the linked PR for embedded sessions_spawn and keep this issue open for the remaining surfaces.
